$comment: Machine-readable inventory of this HarmonyOS capability pack. Read this first, then wire the pieces into your own host. Paths are relative to the pack root (the directory containing this file). Full skill descriptions live in each SKILL.md frontmatter; the summaries here are for routing only.
name: harmony-capability-pack

skills.name: arkts-grammar-standards
skills.summary: ArkTS linter rule dictionary, forbidden syntax, TS-to-ArkTS rewrites, ArkUI structural constraints, Kit API quick reference.
skills.loadWhen: Before writing or modifying the first .ets file of a session.

skills.name: arkts-error-fixes
skills.summary: 30 categories of ArkTS compilation errors, each with a reference note and a runnable counter-example under assets/.
skills.loadWhen: Compilation fails or an ArkTS type error needs fixing.

skills.name: arkts-runtime-fix
skills.summary: JS/ArkTS crash diagnosis: fault-mode library, 8 error-type pattern files, and 5 private Node scripts for faultlogger/hilog evidence collection.
skills.loadWhen: The app crashes, flashes back, or white-screens; a jscrash log or stack trace is available.
skills.patch: HDC calls also treat [Fail] output as failure when the exit code is 0.

skills.name: deveco-create-project
skills.summary: Scaffold a HarmonyOS stage-model project through the local DevEco CLI via copy-template.mjs / detect-sdk.mjs.
skills.loadWhen: Creating, initializing, or scaffolding a new ArkTS project.

skills.name: harmony-build-loop
skills.summary: edit -> arkts_check -> build_project -> start_app orchestration, device/emulator selection, ArkTS hard rules, five build-failure diagnosis categories.
skills.loadWhen: Any session that edits, builds, or runs an ArkTS project.

skills.name: harmony-debug-instrumentation
skills.summary: Hypothesis-driven debugging loop with a greppable [DEBUG][H<id>] log protocol, hdc_log collection, pre-fix/post-fix comparison, and a mandatory cleanup gate.
skills.loadWhen: The app builds and runs but behaves wrong and the bug reproduces on device.

skills.name: harmony-plan-doc
skills.summary: ArkTS planning dimensions (strictness, lifecycle, state, navigation, permissions, resources, performance) and the required sections of a HarmonyOS implementation plan.
skills.loadWhen: Writing an implementation plan or technical design for a HarmonyOS change.

skills.name: harmony-sdd-workflow
skills.summary: Orchestration layer over the five SDD commands: review gates, the backtracking rule, the verification-scope handshake, and the Phase 4/5 delegation contracts.
skills.loadWhen: Running the five-phase SDD workflow end to end instead of invoking the commands one at a time.

skills.name: arkui-component-best-practices
skills.summary: 22 component pattern libraries (swiper, tabs, navigation, list/grid/scroll, stack, input, picker, video, xcomponent and more) plus a keyword search script over them.
skills.loadWhen: Writing, reviewing, or debugging ArkUI component code.

skills.name: arkts-logic-completer
skills.summary: Per-component logic completion references for around 50 ArkUI components, with a five-element checklist covering state declaration, event handling, data binding, and component interaction.
skills.loadWhen: Filling functional logic into a generated or skeletal ArkUI page.

skills.name: repo-understand-skill
skills.summary: Eight-step ArkTS repository comprehension across UI, routing/communication, logic, and data dimensions, including a behavioural-equivalence audit and a structured output format.
skills.loadWhen: Locating functionality or understanding architecture in an unfamiliar ArkTS project.

skills.name: solution-design
skills.summary: Technical design generation with class and sequence diagrams and effort estimation, plus templates for UI pages, network, multimedia, data storage, and device capability.
skills.loadWhen: Producing a module design document or software architecture for a feature.

skills.name: responsive-layout-generator
skills.summary: Converts absolute-position DSL into responsive layout DSL, with breakpoint, chunk, and multi-device layout references.
skills.loadWhen: Turning fixed-position layout data into an adaptive ArkUI layout.

skills.name: arkui2hds
skills.summary: Migrating standard or custom ArkUI components to HDS (UI Design Kit) components, with a complete before/after Tabs migration case.
skills.loadWhen: Replacing ArkUI components with HDS equivalents.

skills.name: d2c-fast
skills.summary: Ten-stage pipeline turning a Pixso design into a complete, high-fidelity HarmonyOS ArkTS page: dual-DSL intake and security screening, pixso-arkts skeleton generation and integration, repo understanding, spec confirmation, best-practice selection, design and component tree, static layout, logic completion, eight quality/system-UI audits, summary.
skills.loadWhen: Converting a Pixso design (link, selected node, or developer-supplied DSL plus local assets) into ArkTS page code.
skills.patch: Host-neutralised: artifact root parameterised, task/general delegation replaced by 'delegate if the host can, otherwise run inline', the run-screenshot requirement mapped onto this pack's tools (new section 13.0), the three input methods split into an MCP-dependent mode and a fully offline mode, six question gates given the fallback upstream never wrote, and three scrubbed sentences plus a self-contradictory artifact path repaired. The two pixso-arkts scripts are byte-identical. Chapter 16's four subagent templates and the ten plan titles are kept verbatim. Full itemised diff in references/host-mapping.md.

skills.name: ui-reconstruction-score
skills.summary: Score UI reconstruction fidelity by comparing a design reference against an implementation screenshot, and surface the most actionable visual/layout problems.
skills.loadWhen: Judging how closely an implemented ArkUI page matches its design reference.
skills.patch: Added a preamble covering the Pillow prerequisite (system pythons often lack it) and a note that the vlm_prompt.md step is an enhancement, not a gate. The upstream agents/openai.yaml is not carried: it binds the DevEco Code IDE front end and the upstream skill loader never reads it. ui_score.py and the three references are byte-identical.

skills.name: arkui-scoring-workflow
skills.summary: Build, deploy, drive and screenshot an ArkUI page, then score it against a design reference through ui-reconstruction-score. Also the numeric backing for d2c-fast's stage 9 edge-band and top-overlap audits.
skills.loadWhen: An ArkUI page is implemented and needs to be compared against its design reference on a real target.
skills.patch: Upstream writes the tool layer as a generic 'MCP tool' because it targets DevEco Code's own tool set. Added a binding table onto this pack's tools (build_project / start_app / perform_ui_action screenshot / get_app_ui_tree / hdc_log), plus get_app_ui_tree as a structural evidence source upstream does not use, and the d2c-fast stage 9 relationship. agents/openai.yaml not carried, same reason as ui-reconstruction-score.

mcp.note: Requires Node >= 20 and `npm install` inside the pack root. DEVECO_HOME / DevEco Studio must be present for build, device, and ArkTS-check tools.

toolGroups.note: arkts_knowledge_search requires a China-site Huawei DevEco login.

Request positions are 1-based everywhere. The aliases also return 1-based positions; `lsp` returns the raw LSP payload, whose positions are 0-based. `lsp` exposes the 9 official operations. find_references and find_call_hierarchy (incoming) load project files mentioning the symbol into the language server before querying, so results are not limited to files opened earlier in the session.

Read and drive the UI of a connected device. The upstream UI auto-verification tools (verify_ui, save_ui_screenshot, get_ui_verification_log) are disabled by this gateway: verify_ui needs a multimodal model this pack does not configure, and the other two are keyed by a verify_ui run id. Calling them returns TOOL_DISABLED. perform_ui_action resolves `hvd` from the connected devices when it is omitted.

Section-structure check for spec.md / plan.md / tasks.md, ported from the upstream spec_write pipeline. Upstream ran it automatically after its own writer; this pack uses the host's write tool, so the SDD commands call it explicitly once the artifact is written. It reports and never blocks.

hostToolMapping.$comment: Tools the upstream commands assumed, which this pack does NOT provide. Map them onto your host's equivalents before running the SDD commands.
hostToolMapping.spec_write: Any file-write tool. Upstream used a dedicated spec artifact writer; the commands here just say 'the host's file-write tool'.
hostToolMapping.question: Your host's ask-the-user mechanism. spec-specify needs it for clarification gates.
hostToolMapping.task: Your host's subagent/delegation mechanism. Optional - the commands run fine single-threaded.
hostToolMapping.read/edit/write/glob/grep: Your host's own file and search tools.

invocationPolicy.$comment: Single source of truth for how hosts may auto-trigger these skills. scripts/install-host.mjs renders it per host: Claude gets `disable-model-invocation: true` in SKILL.md frontmatter, Codex gets `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` in agents/openai.yaml. Never edit the skills under skills/ to express this — they are byte-identical with upstream and tests enforce that.

disableImplicitInvocation.$comment: Skills where merely deciding to load them can cause an irreversible or outward-facing action. The test is the side effect, NOT the manifest category: harmony-build-loop is category `tools` but is pure methodology, and auto-loading it is precisely the point.
disableImplicitInvocation.deveco-create-project: Creates directories and writes a project tree.
disableImplicitInvocation.d2c-fast: Writes generated ArkTS artifacts in bulk.
disableImplicitInvocation.hmos-instrument-test: Runs instrumented tests on a real device.
disableImplicitInvocation.hmos-local-test: Runs tests on a real device.

mcpDependency.$comment: Skills that drive bundled scripts through the deveco-tool MCP. Codex renders these into agents/openai.yaml dependencies.tools so the host can surface the requirement. Derived from the `scripts` field on each skill entry; kept explicit so the installer never has to guess.

excluded.agents: The 11 built-in agent definitions. What was portable is their prompt content: build, plan, debug and goal were harvested into the four `extracted-from-agent-prompt` skills. What is not ported is the harness around them — the permission tables (upstream has no tools allowlist; tool visibility is expressed entirely through permissions), the mode/hidden/temperature configuration, and the plan_enter/plan_exit/debug_exit turn protocols. The remaining 7 agents are generic OpenCode session agents with no HarmonyOS content.
excluded.uiVerification: The UI auto-verification chain. spec-verify ships build-only.
excluded.customizeDeveco: The 5th upstream skill, `customize-deveco`, documents DevEco Code's own config format. Kept under docs/ for reference; not part of the pack.
